newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian leader in Australia cash case resigns.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian leader in Australia cash case resigns.

text.p: A senior Malaysian leader charged with trying to export $940,000 from Australia has resigned as chief minister of Selangor state, the national Bernama news agency said on Saturday.

It quoted Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad as saying that Muhammad Muhammad Taib's resignation would be effective from Monday. Muhammad is facing two charges in a Brisbane court for trying to carry the money out of Australia in cash on December 22.
Muhammad, a vice-president of Malaysia's dominant political party, the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), is considered to be one of the country's most influential men.

"It is his own wish to resign so that any investigation conducted will not affect UMNO's image and we will only consider his position in the party after the decision in Brisbane on whether he is guilty or not," Mahathir was quoted as saying.
Bernama said Muhammad has also resigned as UMNO's liaison chief for Kuala Lumpur and Selangor and as chairman of Barisan Nasional, the ruling alliance, for the two regions.

At a preliminary hearing of the case in Brisbane on Friday Muhammad, charged with failing to declare to customs an amount over A$5,000, was slapped with an additional charge of making a false statement in relation to the declaration.
